mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has risen each of the last three weeks (-22.0 to -20.0). This momentum reflects an ongoing recovery in discretionary mobility that is likely to persist in the near term, producing a higher 4-week mean than the prior 4-week mean.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC improved from -22.0 to -20.0 over 3 consecutive weeks
failure_condition: If the next 4-week mean of RETAIL_REC is lower than the trailing 4-week mean despite the prior 3-week upward trend, the momentum-continuation mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS mobility spiked sharply in the earliest week (55.0) then settled near 44-45 for three weeks, consistent with a one-time seasonal/holiday surge reverting to a stable summer baseline. Once PARKS stabilizes, outdoor-to-indoor substitution effects on RETAIL_REC fade, removing a prior drag and allowing RETAIL_REC to tick upward.
candidate_trigger: PARKS week-on-week change falls below 5 points in absolute value for two consecutive weeks (stabilization threshold)
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS fell from 55.0 to 46.4 then stabilized near 44-45
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC continues to decline or stays flat over the next 2 weeks despite PARKS stabilizing within a narrow band, this stabilization-substitution mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT and WORKPLACES have both remained deeply negative and flat (TRANSIT ~-37 to -38, WORKPLACES ~-22 to -24) over four weeks, indicating commuting-linked mobility is in a low-level equilibrium. Because retail trips are often bundled with commute trips, this joint stagnation should cap any near-term rise in RETAIL_REC, keeping it roughly flat to slightly lower.
evidence_refs: fact:both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES show less than 2-point week-on-week movement for 3 consecutive weeks
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC rises by more than 1 point in the next week while TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both remain flat, the commute-bundling cap mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL time has declined steadily from 6.0 to 3.6 over four weeks, indicating households are spending progressively less time at home. This behavioral unwinding of stay-home patterns is expected to continue and translate into increased out-of-home discretionary activity, raising RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL fell monotonically from 6.0 to 3.6 over 4 weeks
failure_condition: If RESIDENTIAL continues to decline but RETAIL_REC's next 4-week mean is not higher than its trailing 4-week mean, the stay-home-unwinding mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM has remained essentially flat (-16.3 to -16.1) across four weeks, suggesting essential-trip demand has saturated at a stable level. With essential trips no longer a variable driver, any further movement in RETAIL_REC will be driven by discretionary recovery alone, which the recent uptrend suggests will push RETAIL_REC modestly higher.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM week-on-week variation stays within 1 point for 3+ consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM ranged only between -16.3 and -15.3 over 4 weeks
failure_condition: If GROCERY_PHARM remains flat but RETAIL_REC's next 2-week mean falls relative to the prior 2-week mean, the essential-trip-saturation mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT mobility has shown a small but persistent improvement trend (-38.1 to -37.1) without any sudden drop, suggesting no new transit restrictions or lockdown policy has been imposed. In the absence of a policy tightening signal, the existing gradual recovery in RETAIL_REC is expected to continue over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT week-on-week drop exceeds 10 points (would indicate a policy tightening shock)
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT improved slightly and monotonically from -38.1 to -37.1 over 4 weeks
failure_condition: If TRANSIT suddenly drops more than 10 points week-on-week (indicating a new restriction) yet RETAIL_REC still rises, or if TRANSIT stays stable but RETAIL_REC falls, the policy-absence mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: If WORKPLACES mobility were to fall sharply (a threshold crossing of more than 10 points week-on-week decline), this would signal a new business closure wave or renewed restrictions, which would cascade into reduced retail footfall as commuting-linked shopping trips disappear, pulling RETAIL_REC lower over the following two weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES falls more than 10 points week-on-week from its current level near -22
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES has been stable between -22.1 and -23.9 over 4 weeks, so no threshold crossing has yet occurred
failure_condition: If WORKPLACES crosses the -10-point weekly decline threshold but RETAIL_REC's next 2-week mean does not fall relative to its trailing mean, the restriction-cascade mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL and WORKPLACES move in a coupled inverse pattern: as RESIDENTIAL declines (6.0→3.6) while WORKPLACES stays roughly flat, this divergence implies people are leaving home for non-work (discretionary) purposes rather than returning to offices. This discretionary-specific mobility shift should disproportionately boost RETAIL_REC relative to a scenario where both move together, over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL declines while WORKPLACES week-on-week change stays within 2 points (decoupling condition)
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL fell 2.4 points while WORKPLACES varied less than 2 points over the same 4 weeks
failure_condition: If the RESIDENTIAL-WORKPLACES decoupling persists but RETAIL_REC's next 4-week mean does not exceed its trailing 4-week mean, the discretionary-decoupling mechanism is rejected.
